The petitioners - accused Nos.2 to 5 are before this Court challenging the proceeding for the offences punishable under Sections 498A, 323, 504, 506 read with Section 149 of IPC.

The case of the prosecution is that, the accused No.1 is the husband.
The accused No.2 is the mother-in-law.
The accused No.3 is the brother-in-law.
The accused No.4 is the sister-in-law and the accused No.5 is the husband of accused No.4.

They subjected the defacto complainant to cruelty,
and also a demand was made to bring money from the parental home.
The cognizance taken of the aforesaid offences is impugned in this petition.

3. The learned counsel for the petitioners - accused Nos.2 to 5 submits that, except the omnibus and general allegations, there is no specific allegation as against each of the accused herein, and the cognizance taken only on the basis of omnibus allegation is impermissible.

4. On the other hand, the learned counsel for the respondent No.2 - defacto complainant would submit that, there are specific allegations against each of the accused herein subjecting the defacto complainant to cruelty, and also to bring money from the parental home, and the various contentions raised by the petitioners - accused Nos.2 to 5 can be considered only after full fledged trial.
The veracity of the allegation cannot be gone into.
Hence, sought for dismissal of the petition.
5. The learned High Court Government Pleader for the respondent - State would reiterate the submissions of the learned counsel for the respondent No.2.

Perusal of the charge sheet material indicates that, the defacto complainant has alleged that, the accused No.1 and his family members have subjected the defacto complainant to cruelty both mentally and physically, and also a demand was made to bring money from the parental home.

There is no specific allegation as against the accused Nos.2 to 5, who are the family members of the accused No.1 as to how, and in what manner, they subjected the defacto complainant to cruelty both mentally and physically, and also a demand was made to bring money from the parental home,
except the omnibus and general allegations.
7.

The Hon'ble Apex Court in Kahkashan Kausar v. State of Bihar, (2022) 6 SCC 599 has held that,
the relatives of the husband should not be roped in on the basis of omnibus allegations, unless specific instances of their involvement in the crime are made out.

entities.text: Kahkashan Kausar v. State of Bihar, (2022) 6 SCC 599
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text:
In the present case, there is no specific allegation against accused No.2 to 6, who are the family members of the accused No.1,
except general and omnibus allegations to constitute the above offences.
8. Hence, the cognizance taken by the learned Magistrate as against all these accused only on the basis of omnibus and general allegation is impermissible.
The continuation of criminal proceeding against these accused will be an abuse of process of law.

Accordingly, I pass the following:
ORDER i) Criminal petitions stand allowed.

3 ii) The impugned proceeding in CC No.14908/2022 pending on the file of the I Additional Civil Judge and JMFC, Kalaburagi insofar as it relates to the petitioners - accused Nos.2 to 5 is hereby quashed.
iii) The learned Magistrate to proceed against the accused No.1 on the available material on record without being influenced by any of the observations made in this order.
iv) All contentions are kept open.
